result:
task: Rewrite W2-105's acceptance README map (DAEO-zpdj) so that the pinned `gov accept` reads every line, using full node ids, with no change to test code.
status: DONE
work_completed: In each of the three map tables I added a `KPI` column whose cell starts with the lines the row serves: S1, F1 (3 rows), S2, F1, F2 (4 rows) and S3, F3 (6 rows). Each row keeps the lines its section heading gave it before. Every item is now a full node id (`test_w2_105_install_block.py::test_<name>[<real param id>]`) taken from a collect-only run. The 22 placeholder items (`[<install>-deny]`, `[<role>-<install>]`, `× 2`, and the bare `[pip install requests]`) are each written out. Nothing outside the three tables changed.
files_changed: `tests/acceptance/W2-105/README.md`, commit `3341c7328ad0` on w2/W2-105 (19 lines changed each way). No merge, push, amend or rebase.
evidence: Sandbox check, step 0: (a) the write to `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-zpdj` was refused (`OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`); (b) `git hash-object -w` and `git update-index --refresh` both worked (exit 0). Identity: `independent-test-designer` / `DAEO-zpdj`; head at start `19ac51dd9793`, tree clean. `ps` check: no ollama or llama-server process. With the runner's own `parse_map`, `names_a_test` and `matches` run against the 28 collected ids: success-1 8 cases, success-2 14, success-3 6, failure-1 22, failure-2 14, failure-3 6, no unmatched item, 0 unmapped. Scratch: one ids file in the sandbox TMPDIR, removed.
tests: `gov accept DAEO-zpdj` (plain form, `~/.local/bin/gov`) exit 0, outcome pass. Per line, passed/failed/skipped: S1 8/0/0, S2 14/0/0, S3 6/0/0, F1 22/0/0, F2 14/0/0, F3 6/0/0; unmapped 0; totals 28/0/0. Scoped run through `heavy_slot.sh` (it waited for a slot first): 28 passed in 8.73s, exit 0. The `-m "not local_only" -k "not real and not green_here and not time_limit"` exclusion left out no case.
discoveries: (1) The ticket does have S4 and F4 (W1-38 and W1-39 pass on the change), but none of the 28 cases serves them. `gov accept` runs only the ticket's own folder (`_run` passes `str(folder)` to pytest), so a map row naming W1-38 or W1-39 cases would match nothing collected and fail its line (exit 3). I left S4 and F4 without a row; the README's "Success 4, failure 4" section still says those lines are shown by running `tests/acceptance/W1-38` and `W1-39`. (2) The old map was in heading form: the lines read fine, but items like `name[param]` with no `::` never match (`WORD.fullmatch` refuses the bracket), which is why S1, S2, F1 and F2 had 0 cases. (3) `tools/keyword_warn.py` is neither in this tree nor on w2/integrate, so row W2-L423's check could not be run; the edit adds only node ids and line names.
risks: S4 and F4 are not measured by `gov accept DAEO-zpdj`; they rest on separate W1-38 and W1-39 runs, which I did not run here (outside the brief). The rows keep the original designer's broad line assignment, so for example the ask/allow cases still serve S1/F1 rather than also S3/F3, and the orchestrator-asked cases serve F2. That is faithful to the earlier map but loose in places.
lessons: A map item has to carry its file and its exact parameter id (`file.py::test_x[id]`) to match; the README's shorthand (`× 2`, `[<install>]`, a bare `[param]` continuing the previous item) reads well but never matches.
proposed_decisions: none. The S4/F4 question can be settled from the runner as it stands: a cross-folder line cannot be in the map without failing it.
unresolved: Whether S4/F4 should be shown at landing by a W1-38/W1-39 run (CTO, outside the sandbox) rather than by this map.
recommended_next_action: The CTO lands `3341c7328ad0` through the queue as usual, and runs `tests/acceptance/W1-38` and `tests/acceptance/W1-39` on the change as the S4/F4 evidence.
